label: GO step, choosing a2 after a rewarded trial, late in the episode
explanation: Fires only at GO; never at D1 or D2. Within GO it fires almost only when the model picks a2 (model_act==2 holds 99% of the activation mass; a strongly negative choice logit) and the previous trial was rewarded (96% of the mass). It also depends strongly on time in the episode: it is silent before about trial 30, its rate climbs from about trial 50, and it peaks at trials 80-99. Dev F1 is 0.83 with ep_trial>=60 (precision 0.87, mass recall 0.94). Dropping the episode-time condition cuts precision to 0.39. Missed activations are weak: about 6% of the mass, mostly small firings at a2 GO steps after an unrewarded trial. The feature does not fire when the model chooses a1, at any non-GO step, or early in an episode. From the example windows, magnitude seems to grow over runs of consecutive rewarded a2 trials, but I did not quantify this. The predicate uses no future variables: model_act is the policy output of the model itself at GO. The upcoming action (action/next_action) behaves the same way but counts as future at GO.

issues: All factual claims check out on the dev profile. Activity is GO-only: D1 and D2 have 0 active steps. model_act==2 holds 99.1% of the mass. prev_reward==1 holds 96.4%. By ep_trial, there are 0 active steps in trials 0-19 and 2 in trials 20-29; the rate then climbs (trial 50-59 rate 0.022, 60-69 0.071, 80-99 about 0.15). Dropping the ep_trial condition gives precision 0.63 at F1 0.74 (the explanation's 0.39 figure is for a variant I did not reproduce, but the direction holds). The test score reproduces: P 0.866, R 0.778, F1 0.82, mass recall 0.932.

The 'late in the episode' cutoff is a ramp, not a step. Inside the predicate, precision is 0.61 for trials 60-69, 0.91 for 70-79 and 0.98 for 80+. Most false positives are therefore early-60s a2 GO steps. This is a graded effect, not a separate class of counterexamples. Moving the cutoff to ep_trial>=62 barely changes anything (test F1 0.824 vs 0.82).

After a rewarded rare transition (prev_common==0) the feature fires less reliably: precision 0.60 vs 0.92 after a rewarded common one, but this is only about 5% of the mass. After an unrewarded trial: it never fires if that trial was rare (precision 0.001) and fires weakly about 40% of the time if it was common. This matches the claim that the misses are small firings after unrewarded a2 trials (about 3.5% of the mass).

The misses check out (test: 6.8% of the mass, mostly low-magnitude): about 3.5% are a2 GO steps after an unrewarded trial late in the episode, about 1.7% are before trial 60, and about 0.9% are a1 choices. There is no systematic class large enough to justify a new predicate.

Activation tracks a low value-head output (85% of the mass is in the bottom two value bins; the top bin is silent). That is likely the value head reflecting how much of the episode is left, so ep_trial and value are partly interchangeable. A predicate using value<7.13 instead of ep_trial scores lower (F1 0.74), so the ep_trial version is the better one.

The claim that magnitude grows over runs of rewarded a2 trials is not quantified, and it is confounded with the ep_trial ramp (activation rises steadily within a window even across mixed outcomes). Treat it as anecdotal, not part of the label.
No future variables: model_act is the model's own policy output and prev_reward is observed at D1. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
